answer: Operator Liability Ledger. Each identity's actions are tied to a verified operator account through a mirror of its behavioral fingerprint, so duplicates cluster back to one payer. When clustering crosses a fraud threshold, the operator loses a haven for further registrations: all their identities are frozen and the operator, not the wallets, must post a replenishment deposit per clustered identity. Attackers harbor no anonymity advantage because every new identity raises their own exposure, costing a fixed deposit plus loss of existing capacity per duplicate.
